57.notes: Second aorist of λέγω (‘I said’); the DCC lists it separately because of its frequency.

165.notes: Second aorist of ὁράω (‘I saw’); stem ἰδ-.

194.notes: Compound of εἰμί: παρά + εἰμί, ‘be present’.

391.notes: First-declension masculine in -ης (the DCC export labels it 2nd declension).

423.notes: First-declension masculine in -ής (the DCC export labels it 2nd declension).

428.notes: In Attic prose usually middle ἀποκρίνομαι ‘answer’; the aorist passive ἀπεκρίθην is later Greek.

462.notes: Perfect with present meaning (‘I fear’); δέδια is the second-perfect form.

145.notes: First aorist ἔστησα is transitive (‘I set up’), second aorist ἔστην intransitive (‘I stood’); perfect ἕστηκα ‘I stand’.

27.notes: Declined like a 3rd-declension adjective (πᾶς, πᾶσα, πᾶν; gen. παντός, πάσης, παντός); the DCC export files it under irregular nouns.

30.notes: Irregular: nom./acc. sg. masc. and neut. from stem πολυ-, all other forms from πολλ- (πολλοῦ, πολλῷ, πολλοί…).

52.notes: Irregular: nom./acc. sg. masc. and neut. μέγας, μέγαν, μέγα; all other forms from μεγαλ-.

151.notes: Reciprocal pronoun ‘each other’; no nominative, plural (and dual) only.

285.notes: Attic contracted 2nd declension (νόος → νοῦς): νοῦς, νοῦ, νῷ, νοῦν; pl. νοῖ, νῶν, νοῖς, νοῦς.

348.notes: Attic-declension form νεώς (gen. νεώ) is the usual classical spelling; ναός is the common form.

510.notes: Contracted adjective (χάλκεος → χαλκοῦς): all forms circumflexed on the ending.

176.notes: Declined like οὗτος: feminine and neuter plural from τοσαυτ- (τοσαύτη, τοσαῦτα); neuter singular τοσοῦτο or τοσοῦτον.

55.notes: Declined like οὗτος: feminine and neuter plural from τοιαυτ- (τοιαύτη, τοιαῦτα); neuter singular τοιοῦτο or τοιοῦτον.

189.notes: Contracts with η instead of ᾱ: ζῶ, ζῇς, ζῇ, ζῶμεν, ζῆτε, ζῶσι; infinitive ζῆν.

104.notes: Contracts with η instead of ᾱ: χρῶμαι, χρῇ, χρῆται, χρώμεθα, χρῆσθε, χρῶνται; infinitive χρῆσθαι. Takes the dative.

tables.forms: ᾤμην ᾤου ᾤετο ᾠόμεθα ᾤεσθε ᾤοντο
tables.note: Athematic in the singular (ᾤμην, ᾤου, ᾤετο).

171.notes: Present οἴομαι or (in prose) οἶμαι; imperfect ᾤμην; aorist passive in form (ᾠήθην) with active meaning ‘I thought’.

383.notes: The simplex is rare: Attic uses ἀναμιμνῄσκω ‘remind’ and the perfect middle μέμνημαι ‘I remember’ (aorist passive ἐμνήσθην ‘I remembered, mentioned’).

384.notes: The simplex θνῄσκω is poetic; prose uses ἀποθνῄσκω. The perfect τέθνηκα means ‘I am dead’ (short forms τέθναμεν, τεθνάναι, τεθνεώς).
